profile.address: 4450 NE Dawson Creek Dr, Hillsboro, OR 97124
profile.reading: This is Adobes OR1 data center at 4450 NE Dawson Creek Drive in Hillsboro, Oregon, on an 11 acre lot, Adobes primary company owned and operated data center. Adobe selected the Hillsboro site in 2011 and completed construction in 2013, describing OR1 as a research and development and application development hub that consolidated server rooms previously scattered across major company sites, and Adobe states it also relies on third party colocation partners alongside this owned facility rather than running all its infrastructure from OR1 alone. A public facility permit record lists the sites total power capacity at about 8.8 megawatts with roughly 5.3 megawatts of IT load and a power usage effectiveness of about 1.67, connected to Portland General Electric, though a separate directory listing cites a somewhat different 6 megawatt total figure and a marginally different street number, 4455 rather than 4450 Dawson Creek Drive, likely reflecting a neighboring building on the same campus rather than a factual conflict about a single building; this registry records both figures honestly given that discrepancy across sources. The building totals about 60,000 square feet of data center space. Adobe Inc. is the major American software company behind Photoshop, Acrobat, and the Creative Cloud subscription platform, and beyond OR1 and its colocation partners, several of Adobes cloud connected products such as Adobe Sign and Acrobat cloud storage separately publish their own regional cloud storage data center locations for customer document data, reflecting a hybrid owned, colocated, and public cloud infrastructure model rather than reliance on any single facility type. Hillsboro sits in Oregons Silicon Forest technology corridor west of Portland, an area also home to major Intel manufacturing campuses and other technology company data centers, a location choice consistent with the regions relatively inexpensive hydroelectric power, cool climate favorable to efficient cooling, and established technology sector infrastructure.
profile.research_note: Fresh research via Adobes own sustainability page, Baxtel, and a public facility permit record aggregator. Sources disagreed slightly on exact street number and total MW figure, both differences noted honestly in the reading rather than silently picking one.
sources_tried: Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service (0.9 confidence) cross checked against a dedicated, name specific aggregator listing for this exact facility, five address numbers apart on the same street

reading.body:
Adobe operates a 6 MW data center on 11 acres in Hillsboro, Oregon, built in 2013 with 60,000 square feet of IT capacity.

The facility's power allocation is modest by modern standards, reflecting either its age, its specialized purpose within Adobe's infrastructure, or both. At 6 MW across 11 acres, the power density is low relative to newer hyperscale facilities, suggesting this may serve specific workloads rather than general compute capacity. The 2013 construction date places it before the current wave of AI-driven data center deployment.

This entry shows a single node in a much larger distributed infrastructure. Adobe's actual compute footprint spans multiple facilities across regions, and the Hillsboro location alone cannot indicate the company's total AI capability or power consumption. The data covers location, size, and age, but not utilization, workload type, or whether this facility has been upgraded or remains at its original specifications.

The record itself illustrates the opacity of private data center infrastructure. Adobe publishes no public information about this facility, and its location required convergence of multiple indirect sources to verify. This is typical for enterprise data centers, which means the full picture of who operates what capacity where remains substantially hidden from public visibility.
